  "text": "When the reservoir fell that summer, the old road appeared first, running pale and crooked into the mud.

Elsie parked beside the warning sign. Her grandson carried the folding chair she had told him she wouldn’t need.

“Which house was yours?” he asked.

“There aren’t houses now.”

“I meant where.”

She pointed beyond a line of broken posts.

They walked slowly. Small shells cracked under his trainers. Elsie kept to the road, though the fields on either side looked firm enough.

At the bridge, she stopped.

He unfolded the chair.

“I’m not tired.”

“I am,” he said, and sat down.

The stream beneath the bridge was narrow enough to step across. A plastic bottle turned in a pool beside the stonework.

“Your grandad dropped his bicycle here,” she said. “Showing off.”

“Did you know him then?”

“Not officially.”

He waited, but she was looking towards the posts again.

After a while she took a key from her coat pocket. It was tied with string to a brown cardboard label, the writing almost gone.

“Mum says you’ve still got that.”

“Apparently.”

“Does she know you brought it?”

Elsie rubbed a little rust from the teeth with her thumb.

Below them, the bottle knocked against the bridge. Her grandson climbed down and picked it up, letting the water drain before putting it in his bag.

When he returned, she was sitting in the chair.

“Found anything else?” she asked.

“Just that.”

She held out her hand for help getting up. He steadied the chair while she folded it, then took it from her.

The key went back into her pocket."
